sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h4 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i04, first proposed by independent author A. Medium target, Hard
  welcome (user 2026-10-10). The sketch survived the form's quick test (user chat 2026-10-10, one draw, no trace);
  rev 0 keeps the tested wording word for word. A quick-test survival is not a tier; difficulty pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 4 L30: HHS's rule "is effective May 7, 2026" (its Federal Register date is May 11, 2026).
  Doc 4 L26: recipients with fifteen or more employees, May 11, 2027. Doc 4 L143: DOJ's rule applies to State and
  local government entities "regardless of whether those entities also receive Federal financial assistance", and
  some HHS recipients "are also public entities governed by title II". Doc 3 L25: total population of 50,000 or
  more, April 26, 2027. The county has both dates; the earlier is April 26, 2027. May 7, 2026 to April 26, 2027 =
  354 elapsed days.
- Universe: not applicable (single value). No other federal WCAG 2.1 deadline is in the bundle: Doc 1 names WCAG
  2.2 AA as an example standard for grant applicants, Doc 6 sets no web standard.
- Necessity: Doc 4 is the only place that prints May 7, 2026 (grep, all seven texts) and the only one that mentions
  HHS's rule at all; Doc 3 never mentions HHS, section 504 or employees. Doc 3 is the only place that prints
  April 26, 2027 (Doc 4: 0 hits for "April 26" and "April 24"); Doc 4 describes DOJ's change only as "by one year"
  and "now three (3) and four (4) years", which with the public 2024 date gives April 24, 2027 and 352 days, not
  the gold. Stated risk: a solver that recalls DOJ's April 2026 extension itself could supply April 26, 2027
  without Doc 3. No removal probe was run.
- Selected-lever checks: not a which-items question; no rounding or exclusion lever is claimed. Wrong routes
  recomputed (Python datetime, 2026-10-10): HHS's own date 369; counted from the May 11, 2026 Federal Register
  date 350; DOJ date built from "by one year" 352; counted from DOJ's effective date April 20, 2026, 371; later
  tiers 720 (April 26, 2028) and 734 (May 10, 2028); inclusive count 355. None equals 354.
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Linking across documents, picks the wrong entity or section) -> 369: the question
  is framed around HHS (funding, HHS's interim rule) and Doc 4's SUMMARY gives such a recipient May 11, 2027; the
  county has to be recognised as a State and local government entity under Doc 3 as well, whose date is 15 days
  earlier. Mode 2 (Document convention, uses the wrong period or date) -> 350: Doc 4's header and citation line
  carry its Federal Register date, Monday, May 11, 2026, which is also the old compliance date; the DATES line
  gives the effective date, May 7. Considered and not declared: the "by one year" route (352), which needs Doc 3 to
  be skipped, and the later tiers, which the stated population and staff rule out. Unmeasured: the quick test gave
  no trace, so offer to re-declare from observed wrong answers if a difficulty run arrives before Submit.
- Calculation verification: Python datetime 2026-10-10: date(2027,4,26) - date(2026,5,7) = 354. Second route: 24
  days left in May 2026, then June to December 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 = 214, January to March 2027
  31 + 28 + 31 = 90, plus 26 days of April: 24 + 214 + 90 + 26 = 354. Convention: elapsed days ("days after"),
  start day excluded; no February 29 in the span. The reasoning's route (365 - 11) gives the same.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: 354 is printed nowhere as a day count (grep). The page overview lists Doc 3's and
  Doc 4's dates separately and states no gap. Shortest route: three SUMMARY/DATES lookups, the earlier of two
  dates, one date gap.
- Precision/readings: "took effect" is the effective date Doc 4 states (May 7, 2026), not its publication date.
  "First meet WCAG 2.1" is the earlier of the two compliance dates binding the county; both rules adopt WCAG 2.1
  (Doc 3 L63, Doc 4 L59). A county is not a special district government, so Doc 3's first tier applies on the
  stated population. The staff size only fixes HHS's date at May 11, 2027; with fewer than fifteen employees
  DOJ's date would still come first.
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (notes/intake.json; notes/doc-map.md).
- Style/set review: 28 words. q01 (same document pair, cost figures, no shared input) is dropped. Sketch i06 uses
  the same anchor and DOJ date and must not be submitted beside q02. Words a paraphrase must keep: HHS-funded;
  county; 50,000 or more people; 15 or more employees; "after HHS's interim rule took effect"; "first"; days.
- Warnings answered: rev 0 floor 2026-10-10: 0 FAIL, 1 WARN. WARN origin: origin: claude is the actual writer; the
  export sheet takes origin user only, reported as is. The emulated form number check raised nothing: every date
  and threshold in Steps 1 to 4 is printed in its cited document before character 17,500, and Steps 5 to 7 are

sections.question: An HHS-funded county has 50,000 or more people and 15 or more employees. How many days after HHS's interim rule took effect must it first meet WCAG 2.1?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 4, DATES): HHS's interim rule is effective May 7, 2026.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 4, SUMMARY): for recipients of HHS assistance with fifteen (15) or more employees, the date for meeting the web accessibility requirements, which adopt WCAG 2.1, is extended from May 11, 2026, to May 11, 2027.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, SUMMARY): for State and local government entities with a total population of 50,000 or more, the Justice Department's compliance date for the same WCAG 2.1 requirements is extended from April 24, 2026, to April 26, 2027.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 3 and Doc 4, coverage): Doc 4 says the Justice Department's rule applies to State and local government entities whether or not they receive Federal financial assistance, and that some recipients of HHS assistance are also public entities under that rule. The county is one of them, so it has both dates, and April 26, 2027 comes before May 11, 2027: the Justice Department's date is the one it must meet first.

Step 5. Calculation (Doc 3 and Doc 4): 12 months of 30 days each, in days: 12 × 30 = 360.

Step 6. Calculation (Doc 3 and Doc 4): a common year is 5 days longer than that, and no leap day falls between May 7, 2026 and May 7, 2027, so that year has, in days: 360 + 5 = 365.

Step 7. Final answer (Doc 3 and Doc 4): April 26, 2027 falls 11 days before May 7, 2027, so the days from May 7, 2026 to April 26, 2027 are: 365 - 11 = 354.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Picks the wrong entity or section

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Document convention
How a careless solver fails: Uses the wrong period or date

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 4's SUMMARY sets May 11, 2027 for such recipients, but the county is also a Doc 3 public entity due April 26, 2027; HHS's date gives 369 days. Document convention: Doc 4 is dated May 11, 2026 but effective May 7; its date gives 350.
